ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Lili Boulanger — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Ms. Boulanger is six months into risankizumab, with two maintenance doses given, the second at home, and the next due in two weeks. She has one or two formed stools a day, no pain, and no extra-intestinal symptoms (Harvey-Bradshaw Index 1). She has regained 5.6 kg since diagnosis. She is composing a new choral work. She asked about having children one day and how her treatment would affect a pregnancy. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1915-08-03; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: No erythema nodosum; injection sites clear

Crohn disease of the terminal ileum and colon (ileocolitis), Montreal A2 L3 B1 without perianal disease, moderate to severe: deep ileal ulcers over 15 cm and patchy colonic ulcers, SES-CD 14, Harvey-Bradshaw Index 11; intestinal tuberculosis excluded by negative interferon-gamma release assay, normal chest X-ray, and biopsies negative for acid-fast bacilli, TB PCR, and mycobacterial culture; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented chronic intestinal illness, whose historical diagnosis is not settled

S — Synthetic diagnosis confirmed within the modern episode; her historical illness is documented (D), but whether it was intestinal tuberculosis or Crohn disease remains a retrospective interpretation (R) and is disputed.

Four months of crampy right lower abdominal pain, loose stools up to six times a day including at night, low-grade evening fevers, and loss of 6 kg; inflammatory markers raised; colonoscopy and small-bowel imaging booked
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis; the documented symptoms of early 1915 are echoed (D).
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic intestinal blood loss and poor absorption (hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, MCV 76, ferritin 9)
S — Synthetic finding at presentation; corrected by intravenous iron.
Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition: BMI 17.6 after losing 6 kg (12 percent of body weight) in four months; albumin 3.3 g/dL
S — Synthetic nutritional status at presentation; resolved with treatment and dietitian support.
Long-term use of risankizumab, an immunosuppressive biologic, for Crohn disease
Acute norovirus gastroenteritis on risankizumab, with mild dehydration; distinguished from a Crohn flare by the sudden onset, household contacts, and a positive stool PCR; resolved in three days
S — Synthetic common infection that teaches the difference between infection and a flare in treated Crohn disease; it does not echo a documented illness.

list.item:
Crohn disease in clinical and biochemical remission (K50.80). Harvey-Bradshaw Index 1, CRP 2 mg/L, and fecal calprotectin 42 ug/g, normal: the six-month targets are met. Endoscopic healing remains to be confirmed. [S]
Continue risankizumab 360 mg every 8 weeks.
Ileocolonoscopy in about two months.
Vitamin B12 yearly because the terminal ileum is involved; 340 pg/mL today.

Malnutrition, resolved (E44.0). Weight 50.6 kg (BMI 19.8) and albumin 4.3 g/dL. [S]
Supplements stopped; normal varied diet.

Future pregnancy. Fertility is normal in Crohn disease in remission. Active disease, not the medicine, is the main risk to a pregnancy. Data on risankizumab in pregnancy are limited, unlike anti-TNF drugs; if she plans a pregnancy, the options will be reviewed with her first. [S]
Plan pregnancy after at least three to six months of steroid-free remission, with a preconception IBD review.
Folic acid 400 micrograms daily from three months before trying.
Effective contraception until then if she becomes sexually active.

list.item: Reach a diagnosis, with tuberculosis excluded, within two weeks. Outcome by 1915-01-28: Ileocolonoscopy, biopsies, MR enterography, interferon-gamma release assay, and chest X-ray completed in nine days; Crohn disease diagnosed and intestinal tuberculosis made very unlikely, with the mycobacterial culture still pending [S]
Steroid-free clinical remission by week 12 to 16 of treatment. Outcome by 1915-04-27: Harvey-Bradshaw Index 2 at week 12, five weeks after the prednisone taper ended [S]
Normal CRP and fecal calprotectin by six months, and endoscopic response at six to twelve months. In progress; target 1915-10-05 [S]
Regain weight to a BMI of 19 or more and correct iron and vitamin D. Outcome by 1915-08-03: Weight 50.6 kg (BMI 19.8); hemoglobin 13.1, ferritin 72, vitamin D 34 [S]
Perform her March concert and keep composing through treatment. Outcome by 1915-04-27: Composing most mornings; the concert went ahead in late March with a plan for bathroom access [S]
